title: Combinatorics Investigation Starter
subject: Combinatorics
summary: A finite-permutation scaffold for exploring fixed points, inversions, descents, derangements, and parity through exact enumeration.
details: This starter helps an instructor build a combinatorics Class around permutations of finite labeled sets. It emphasizes exact definitions and hand-checkable examples before students use bounded enumeration to form and refute conjectures.

objectives: Interpret one-line notation as a bijection rather than an arbitrary sequence.
Compute fixed-point, inversion, and descent statistics from explicit definitions.
Relate derangement and parity properties to exact finite counts.
Form conjectures from enumerated evidence and preserve counterexamples that expose missing hypotheses.

concepts.title: Permutation in one-line notation
concepts.plain_language: A permutation rearranges the labels 1 through n so that every label appears exactly once.
concepts.formal_definition: A permutation of [n]={1,…,n} is a bijection π:[n]→[n]. Its one-line notation is [π(1),…,π(n)].

steps: Check that 1, 2, and 3 each occur exactly once.

nonexample.prompt: The sequence [1,1,2] as a permutation of [3].
nonexample.explanation: The label 1 repeats and 3 is missing, so the rule is not bijective.

concepts.title: Fixed-point count
concepts.plain_language: A fixed point is a position whose label did not move; the invariant counts such positions.

notation.meaning: the set of fixed positions of π

steps: Positions 3 and 4 contain their own labels.

nonexample.prompt: Count the value 1 in [2,1,3] as fixed because it appears.
nonexample.explanation: A fixed point requires π(i)=i. Here the value 1 is in position 2, so it is not fixed.

concepts.title: Inversion count
concepts.plain_language: An inversion is a pair of positions that appears in the opposite order from increasing order.
concepts.formal_definition: For π∈Sₙ, Inv(π)={(i,j):1≤i<j≤n and π(i)>π(j)} and inversion_count(π)=|Inv(π)|.

notation.meaning: an ordered pair of positions with i before j
the set of inversions of π

steps: Pairs (1,3) and (2,3) are inversions because 2>1 and 3>1.

nonexample.prompt: Count (2,1) as a second orientation of the same inversion.
nonexample.explanation: The definition requires i<j, so each positional pair is considered once.

concepts.title: Descent count
concepts.plain_language: A descent occurs when one entry is immediately followed by a smaller entry.

notation.meaning: the positions at which adjacent values decrease

nonexample.explanation: Those values are not adjacent. They form an inversion, but not a descent.

concepts.title: Derangement
concepts.plain_language: A derangement is a permutation in which no label remains in its original position.
concepts.formal_definition: A permutation π∈Sₙ is a derangement when π(i)≠i for every i∈[n], equivalently fixed_point_count(π)=0.

notation.meaning: position i does not contain its original label
the set or number of derangements of [n], according to context

steps: Compare each value with its position.

nonexample.explanation: Position 3 is fixed, so the permutation is not a derangement.

concepts.title: Even permutation
concepts.plain_language: A permutation is even when its inversion count is even.
concepts.formal_definition: A permutation π∈Sₙ is even when inversion_count(π)≡0 (mod 2).

notation.meaning: has remainder zero after division by 2
an equivalent sign convention for an even permutation

nonexample.explanation: It has exactly one inversion, so it is odd rather than even.

object_family.label: Permutations of finite labeled sets
object_family.scope: All permutations of [n] for instructor-approved n with 1≤n≤9.
object_family.representation: one-line array containing each integer from 1 through n exactly once
